name: dense-fleet
_comment: Built to saturate the SCHEDULER, where web_fleet saturates the rig.
Two properties differ from web_fleet, both deliberate:
1. ~44 allocations per job, against web_fleet's 6. The density axis
(--allocs-per-node) scales job COUNT, so every density point on
web_fleet is also a submission-rate point, and the driver -- a
2-vCPU loadgen box spawning one CLI process per submit -- reaches
its ceiling long before the control plane reaches its own. Fat
jobs move the load from submission into placement, which is the
thing under test.
2. Small resource requests (50 mCPU / 64 MiB against 500 / 1024).
web_fleet's api job fits ~16 allocations on an 8-core node, so a
density sweep past that measures capacity exhaustion -- a correct
refusal to place -- rather than scheduler throughput. At 50 mCPU a
5,000-node fleet has room for ~800k allocations, so the sweep ends
when the scheduler stops keeping up and not before.
A 50-replica service into one pool is also precisely the shape that
plan-apply-conflict-reduction targets: decouple_plan_components used
to collapse exactly this to a single candidate per placement.
node_profiles are web_fleet's, unchanged, so fleet shape stays
comparable across the two scenarios.
